angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 542,646 km at 59.27 pc = 0.12 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 16.8709 +/- 0.0125 mas (same row, RUWE 1.13): 59.27 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.78 +/- 0.036 solar radii from Hobson et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-286 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.216H/abstract): 542,646 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.832 +/- 0.049 solar masses from Hobson et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-286 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.216H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5152 +/- 12 K from Hobson et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-286 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.216H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hobson et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-286 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.216H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-286.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.574, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
